description:
FILED s458al (agent AL, round 15) â the second half of #851.  Half (a) is DONE
in the same session (p-high-capture: $21+ is no longer an unbound symbol).

perl makes every capture variable READ-ONLY, and a write is a trappable
run-time death.  Probed 5.40.3 vs ./runpcl on one file, after a
`"abc" =~ /(a)(b)/`:

                              perl                                    PCL
  eval { $1 = 5 }             Modification of a read-only value ...   no error
  eval { chop $1 }            Modification of a read-only value ...   no error
  eval { $1 .= "x" }          Modification of a read-only value ...   no error
  eval { $99 = 5 }            Modification of a read-only value ...   no error
  eval { my $r=\$99; $$r=3 }  Modification of a read-only value ...   no error
  eval { open $1, "foo" }     no error (a DEFINED value is a symbolic no error
                              filehandle name, not an autovivification)
  eval { open $99, "foo" }    Modification of a read-only value ...   no error

Note the last two: perl dies on `open $99` and NOT on `open $1`, because the
difference is autovivification â `open` writes a glob into an UNDEF scalar, and
$99 is undef.  So the family is not "open rejects captures", it is "a write to
a capture dies", with `open`'s write being conditional.

WHY IT IS NOT A SMALL FIX: $1..$20 are plain `defvar` specials holding a string
or *p-undef* â not boxes â so there is no place to hang a read-only flag, and
the write spellings are the whole assign/modify family (`=`, `.=`, `++`, chop,
chomp, s///, tr///, open, substr-lvalue, `\$1` then `$$r =`, `foreach $1`).
The honest shapes are (i) make a capture a read-only BOX (touches the box model
-- coordinate with whoever owns it), or (ii) a compiler rule "a capture
variable in a WRITTEN operand position lowers to a run-time read-only die",
which needs a written-position oracle the compiler does not have today
(`writes_args` is about @_ aliasing in user subs, not builtin write slots).
Measure which spellings actually occur before choosing.

BAR: t/io/open.t row 140 ("readonly fh") -- still failing after #851 half (a),
though the file no longer carries `unbound:$99` as its `sig` and now runs past
line 362.

NOTE (s458al, the trade half (a) made): before half (a), `$99 = 5` killed
the whole FILE at load with an unbound-variable crash; now it is a silent
no-op, exactly like `$1 = 5` has always been (p-setf falls through to
`box-set` on a value that is not a box, which does nothing).  So the two
spellings are consistent and neither is perl -- the loudness that was there
was a compiler artifact, not a diagnosis.  This task is what makes both
right.


=== DESIGN FINDING, s459an (agent AN, round 16).  NOT shipped; measured and
=== sized instead, per the round's brief ("if a clean mechanism exists ship
=== it; otherwise write the design finding and move on -- do NOT scatter
=== per-spelling guards").  The task's own instruction was "measure which
=== spellings actually occur before choosing", so that is what was done.

(1) THE WRITE FAMILY IS THREE SPELLINGS, NOT THE WHOLE ASSIGN/MODIFY SET.
Scanned 1247 files -- perl-tests/, lib/, cpan-tests/modules/, and perl's own
t/ -- for every spelling this task lists:

    $N = ...                 23   (perl-tests/undef.t:58 `eval { $1 = undef }`)
    $N =~ s/// or tr///      10   (perl-tests/tr.t:631 `$1 =~ tr/A-Z//`)
    open $N                   1   (t/io/open.t:362 `eval { open $99, "foo" }`)
    chop $N / chomp $N        0
    $N++ / $N--               0
    $N .= / += / x= ...       0
    foreach $N (...)          0
    substr($N,...) = ...      0
    \$N  (then $$r = ...)     0   -- a raw grep says 237, and ALL of them are
                                     an ESCAPED `\$1` inside a double-quoted
                                     string (test descriptions, and
                                     t/re/pat_re_eval.t's expected-output
                                     strings).  Refined to expression position
                                     the count is 15, and those 15 are the same
                                     escaped-string hits.  ZERO real ones.

And note WHAT the 23 + 10 + 1 mostly are: `eval { ... }` wrappers in tests OF
this very behaviour.  There is no measured CPAN code that writes a capture by
accident; the population is the conformance rows themselves.

(2) WHY THE WRITE IS SILENT TODAY, exactly.  Every spelling lowers to a form
that receives the bare special's VALUE, never a place:

    $1 = 5           ->  (p-scalar-= $1 5)
    $1 =~ s/a/z/     ->  (p-=~ $1 (p-subst "a" "z"))
    open $1, ...     ->  (p-open $1 "<" "/nope")
    chop $1          ->  (p-chop $1)

`%set-cap` does `(setf $1 (subseq str rs re))`, so `$1` holds a raw STRING.
The runtime therefore gets a string where it expects a box: it cannot write,
and it cannot tell a capture from any other non-box value.  That is the whole
bug.  (The s/// path already NOTICES -- it prints `warning: Cannot modify
non-boxed value in s///` on stderr -- but it is generic, it is a warning rather
than a death, and being a RUN-TIME stderr line it is the shape s458al measured
as costing `fresh_perl_is(...,'')` rows; see #874.)

(3) THE TWO SHAPES, RE-SIZED.

  (i) READ-ONLY BOX / MAGIC CELL.  Clean, and the mechanism already exists
      (p-magic-cell, kind :lvalue, is what \substr / \pos / \vec use; a setter
      that signals is one line).  A capture would become a box holding a cell
      whose getter returns the group and whose setter dies -- and then EVERY
      write path, including `\$1` + `$$r = ...` and anything added later, hits
      the one chokepoint the box model already has.
      COST, and why it is not filler-sized: it changes the REPRESENTATION of
      $1..$20, so `%set-cap`, `clear-capture-groups`, `*p-capture-syms*`,
      `local $1`, `p-high-capture` and `@{^CAPTURE}` all move together, and
      every capture READ becomes unbox -> getter funcall.  Capture reads are a
      hot path (`while (/(\d+)/g) { $sum += $1 }`), so this owes a Target-A
      measurement before it is chosen.  It is also squarely in the box/aggregate
      region of cl/pcl-runtime.lisp.

  (ii) A COMPILER RULE at the written slot.  The task called this blocked on
      "a written-position oracle the compiler does not have".  The measurement
      says the oracle needed is THREE SLOTS, all of which the emitter already
      writes by name:
        - the target of `p-scalar-=` / `p-setf`
        - the target of `p-=~` when the RHS is a substitution or transliteration
        - the handle slot of `p-open`
      plus ONE predicate -- "is this CLForm a capture read?" -- which is
      `$1..$20` as a bare symbol or `(p-high-capture N)`, i.e. exactly the two
      shapes Pl::ExprToCL already emits for a capture (the `$SPECIAL_VARS` hit
      and the `^\$([0-9]+)$` branch beside it).  Nothing else in the family
      occurs, so nothing else needs covering, and NOTHING in the box model or
      the read path changes.

      ONE WRINKLE, and it is perl's, not ours: `open $1` does NOT die when $1
      is DEFINED (a defined value is a symbolic filehandle name), while
      `open $99` DOES, because $99 is undef and `open` would have to
      autovivify a glob into it.  So the open slot's check is
      runtime-conditional and wants a two-line runtime helper rather than a
      compile-time die; the other two slots are unconditional.
      MEASURED both ways in this session, perl vs PCL, and PCL says "no error"
      to all six.

RECOMMENDATION: (ii), sized as one predicate + three slots + one runtime
helper for `open`.  (i) is the more principled answer and should be revisited
only if the capture representation moves for another reason -- it is a
box-model change with a hot-path cost, for a family the corpus says is three
spellings deep.

BAR (unchanged): t/io/open.t row 140 ("readonly fh"), plus the six probe lines
above vs perl, plus the `eval { $1 = undef }` rows in perl-tests/undef.t.
Whichever shape is chosen, the death must be TRAPPABLE (every occurrence in
the corpus is inside an `eval`), and it must not become a run-time stderr line
-- that is the #874 lesson, measured in this same session.


=== SHIPPED s460ap (agent AP, round 17), option (ii) as the s459an sizing
=== recommends -- but with TWO of the three slots, not three, and the third
=== RE-SIZED by measurement.  #873 CLOSED; the `=~` half is task #911.

WHAT SHIPPED.  ONE compiler predicate + TWO write slots + TWO runtime helpers.
  - `Pl::ExprToCL::_capture_read_group($flat)` -- the group number when the
    emitted operand is a capture READ, else undef.  Exactly two spellings and
    gen_symbol_form is the only source of either: the bare defvar `$N` for
    $1..$20 and `(p-high-capture N)` for $21+.  Nothing on the read path
    changes; only a WRITE asks.
  - Slot 1, the `=` lowering: a capture target lowers to `(p-capture-write
    RHS)`.  It sits ABOVE the whole place dispatch, because `$1 = â¦` was
    picking the p-scalar-= arm and `$99 = â¦` the generic p-setf tail and BOTH
    were silent no-ops.
  - Slot 3, `open`'s handle argument: wrapped in `(p-capture-fh â¦)`.
  - Runtime `p-capture-write` (croaks through the EXISTING
    %p-readonly-modification, so the text is perl's byte for byte and it is
    trappable) and `p-capture-fh` (the identity on a DEFINED value, croak
    otherwise) -- perl's own rule, since the difference is autovivification.
    VALUE is an ARGUMENT to p-capture-write rather than dropped at the call
    site, so RHS side effects happen BEFORE the death, as perl's sv_setsv.

SLOT 2 (`=~` WITH s/// OR tr///) IS NOT SHIPPED, AND THE MEASUREMENT IS WHY.
It was written, then REVERTED when corpus-diff showed perl-tests/tr.t moving.
perl does NOT die on every s///-or-tr/// against a capture; it decides at RUN
time, and tr.t asserts the exceptions BY NAME.  Probed 5.40.3, 15 rows:
    tr/abcd//        count                no error   (tr.t:748 "explicit read-only count")
    tr/abcd/abcd/    identical            no error   (tr.t:752 "implicit read-only count")
    tr/abcd//c       complement, no repl  no error
    tr///            empty search         no error
    tr/a-z/A-Z/r     /r returns a copy    no error
    tr/a-z/A-Z/      modifies             DIES
    tr/a-z//d        deletes              DIES
    tr/a-z//s        squeezes             DIES
    tr/abcd/ab/      short replacement    DIES
    s/b/z/           matches              DIES
    s/zzz/q/         NO MATCH             no error   <-- run-time, not compile-time
    s/b/z/r          /r                   no error
    m/b/             read                 no error
A compile-time die would have broken tr.t rows 631/639/748/752 ("harmless if
explicitly not updating").  The right place is the runtime's TWO EXISTING
write sites -- cl/pcl-runtime.lisp's `warn "Cannot modify non-boxed value in
s///"` and its tr/// twin, which already fire exactly when a write is needed
and whose tr arm already implements perl's "only if the result differs" rule.
Turning those warns into a death needs an audit of what ELSE reaches them with
a non-box target; that is task #911, filed with this table.

ALSO NOT COVERED, and measured to be empty in the corpus (the s459an scan):
`.=` / `++` / `--` / chop / chomp / substr-lvalue / foreach / `\$1` -- zero
real occurrences across 1247 files.  They stay silent no-ops.

BAR MET.  16 probe rows BYTE-IDENTICAL to perl including the conditional pair
(`open $1` no error, `open $99` dies) and every read path.  The named bar,
t/io/open.t row 140 "readonly fh", PASSES: io/open.t 153/35 -> 154/34,
measured against a base-tree run of the same file.  perl-tests/undef.t's
`eval { $1 = undef }` row passes too (30 -> 31) -- it was a REGISTERED SKIP,
the stale-detector said so in the same run ("REGISTRY-STALE: undef.t test 17
now passes"), and the registry entry was removed in the same commit.
t/op/undef.t 32/5 -> 33/4.  comp/parser.t carries the shape
(`eval{$1=eval{a:}}`) and does not move: 50/48 on both trees.

A PROBE TRAP WORTH KEEPING: the reporter sub must not use s///.  PCL's capture
variables are not block-scoped, so a substitution inside a helper clobbers the
very captures under test -- the first version of the probe read `$1` as empty
everywhere and looked like a regression.  (perl restores $1 on block exit;
that gap is separate and untouched here.)

GUARD: Pl/t/caret-vars-01.t rows 7-8 (6 -> 8) -- the file whose subject is
already "box-set silently returns when its place is not a p-box, so the write
stored nothing" (#565, $^R).  Row 7 = the five dying/not-dying slots via the
file's `both_agree` helper (live perl as oracle); row 8 = the INVERSE (capture
reads everywhere, non-capture writes, $0 still writable), which passes on the
base tree.  Inverse-verified: 7 fails on base, 8 passes.
subject: Capture variables are WRITABLE under PCL; perl says "Modification of a read-only value attempted" (#851 half b)
